experiment_design.technical_details: This experiment tests the hypothesis that the macroscopic arrow of time emerges from statistical entropy increase given a low-entropy initial condition. We will simulate an isolated 2D hard-disk gas system (N=1000 particles) using molecular dynamics. The system is initialized in a low-entropy state (all particles confined to one quadrant with randomized velocities). We track Boltzmann entropy S(t) = k_B ln(Ω(t)) over time. Two scenarios are run: (1) Forward evolution from low entropy, expecting monotonic S(t) increase; (2) Time-reversed evolution from equilibrium, expecting no spontaneous decrease in S(t) without external intervention. The 'flow' of time is operationalized as the gradient dS/dt > 0.

datasets.source: Synthetic data generated via Molecular Dynamics simulation of hard-disk gas. Initial conditions: N=1000 disks, radius r=0.01L, box size LxL. Low-entropy state: particles confined to x < L/2. Equilibrium state: uniform distribution.
datasets.target: Time-series data of Boltzmann entropy S(t), particle position distributions, and velocity autocorrelation functions.

experiment_design.methods: 1. Molecular Dynamics Integration: Use Velocity Verlet algorithm for time integration of Newton's equations for hard-sphere collisions. 2. Entropy Calculation: Estimate phase space volume Ω(t) by binning position-momentum space and calculating Shannon entropy of the distribution, approximating Boltzmann entropy. 3. Time-Reversal Test: At t_equilibrium, reverse all velocity vectors (v -> -v) and continue simulation to check if the system returns to the low-entropy state or remains near equilibrium due to numerical chaos/rounding errors (testing Loschmidt's paradox resolution).

baselines: Random Walk Model: A non-interacting particle model where entropy increases purely due to diffusion, serving as a baseline for non-correlated systems.
Equilibrium Control: A system initialized at maximum entropy (uniform distribution) to verify that dS/dt ≈ 0 on average, confirming no inherent arrow without gradient.
metrics: Entropy Growth Rate: Slope of S(t) vs t during the relaxation phase.
Recurrence Time: Time taken for the system to return to within 5% of initial low-entropy state (if applicable).
Time-Asymmetry Index: Correlation coefficient between forward trajectory S(t) and backward trajectory S(-t).
experiments.ablation: Vary particle number N (100, 500, 1000) to test finite-size effects on entropy fluctuation magnitude. Vary initial confinement ratio (1/4, 1/2, 3/4 of box) to test dependence on initial entropy gap.
experiments.validation_protocol: Verify energy conservation (ΔE/E < 1e-6) to ensure isolation. Check Liouville's theorem compliance by monitoring phase-space volume preservation in fine-grained description vs coarse-grained entropy increase.

datasets.source: Synthetic data generated via Molecular Dynamics simulation of hard-disk gas. Initial conditions: N=1000 disks, radius r=0.01L, box size LxL. Low-entropy state: particles confined to x < L/2. Equilibrium state: uniform distribution.
datasets.target: Time-series data of Boltzmann entropy S(t), particle position distributions, and velocity autocorrelation functions.

experiment_design.methods: 1. Molecular Dynamics Integration: Use Velocity Verlet algorithm for time integration of Newton's equations for hard-sphere collisions. 2. Entropy Calculation: Estimate phase space volume Ω(t) by binning position-momentum space and calculating Shannon entropy of the distribution, approximating Boltzmann entropy. 3. Time-Reversal Test: At t_equilibrium, reverse all velocity vectors (v -> -v) and continue simulation to check if the system returns to the low-entropy state or remains near equilibrium due to numerical chaos/rounding errors (testing Loschmidt's paradox resolution).

baselines: Random Walk Model: A non-interacting particle model where entropy increases purely due to diffusion, serving as a baseline for non-correlated systems.
Equilibrium Control: A system initialized at maximum entropy (uniform distribution) to verify that dS/dt ≈ 0 on average, confirming no inherent arrow without gradient.
metrics: Entropy Growth Rate: Slope of S(t) vs t during the relaxation phase.
Recurrence Time: Time taken for the system to return to within 5% of initial low-entropy state (if applicable).
Time-Asymmetry Index: Correlation coefficient between forward trajectory S(t) and backward trajectory S(-t).
experiments.ablation: Vary particle number N (100, 500, 1000) to test finite-size effects on entropy fluctuation magnitude. Vary initial confinement ratio (1/4, 1/2, 3/4 of box) to test dependence on initial entropy gap.
experiments.validation_protocol: Verify energy conservation (ΔE/E < 1e-6) to ensure isolation. Check Liouville's theorem compliance by monitoring phase-space volume preservation in fine-grained description vs coarse-grained entropy increase.

Two scenarios are run: (1) Forward evolution from low entropy, expecting monotonic S(t) increase; (2) Time-reversed evolution from equilibrium, expecting no spontaneous decrease in S(t) without external intervention.
